block.wareworks.stacker_crane.tooltip.be: The _first aisle_ runs in the direction you look. Connect a _shaft_ to the _bottom_; shafts and cogs at the sides do not connect. A _wrench_ turns it only while the crane is _idle_ and _empty_.

Carries out the controller's _jobs_. On a _corner_ or a _junction_ the whole machine swings a _quarter turn_ and drives on, and where the rails offer more than one way it takes the _cheapest_ one. Faster _rotation_ moves the crane faster; without rotation or when _overstressed_ it _pauses_ where it is and continues later.
Hold _Right-Click_ on the _value panel_ to set the _mast height_: how many _levels_ the crane reaches.
Shows the _size_ of the warehouse, the _mast height_, which _aisle_ the machine is on, whether a _controller_ is linked, the current _job_ and the _held items_.
block.wareworks.stacker_crane.tooltip.su: The _dock_ of a _stacker crane_. The crane travels the _warehouse rails_ in front of it — around _corners_ and through _junctions_ as well — and _stores_ and _retrieves_ items for the _warehouse controller_ behind it.
block.wareworks.warehouse_controller.too: Place it directly _behind_ a _stacker crane_ while looking at the crane; the _display_ faces you.
Hold _Right-Click_ on the _value panel_ to set the letter of the _first aisle_, used in addresses such as _A-03-07R_; every further aisle takes the _next free_ letter.

Shows the _status_, the _size_ of the warehouse and its _aisles_, where the rails _stop_ and why, the number of _storage locations_, _stations_ and _misaligned_ blocks, the _stored items_, the _crane's job_ and the last _planning result_.

Manages one _warehouse_: it gives every _aisle_ of it a _letter_, finds its _storage locations_ and _stations_, keeps _count_ of the stored items and _plans_ the _stacker crane's_ jobs. It never moves items itself.
block.wareworks.warehouse_home_point.too: The _plate_ faces you: stand in the _aisle_ and place it into a _rack_ beside the aisle, like every other station. It holds _no items_ and the crane never stops here for one.

After a short wait the crane drives back and waits in front of this block. The trip is _interrupted_ by the next job the moment there is one, even in the middle of a _corner_, so it never costs you anything — and it holds _no chunks_ loaded.
Nothing happens: on a single aisle the crane stays exactly where it is, which is what it always did. A home point earns its keep the moment your warehouse _bends_.

A warehouse has _one crane_, so it has _one home_. Any further home point lights up _red_ and says so; the same happens to one the crane cannot _drive to_, for instance because a rail between them is broken or _closed_. Break the home point and the _dock_ is home again.
Shows its _address_ and whether the crane really waits here — and if it does not, _why_ not.
When the crane has nothing to do
When the warehouse is one straight aisle
When there is more than one

Marks where the _stacker crane_ waits when it has nothing to do. Put it beside the _rails_ where the next job usually starts — next to your _terminal_, next to an _input_ — and the machine comes back here instead of standing wherever its last job ended.
The _opening_ faces you: stand in the _aisle_ and place it into a _rack_ beside the aisle.
Accepts items from _belts_, _funnels_, _chutes_, _hoppers_ and _Mechanical Arms_. The _stacker crane_ carries them to a free _storage location_; automation can only _insert_, never take items out.
A _station_ of a warehouse _aisle_ where items _enter_ the warehouse. It _buffers_ arriving items until a _stacker crane_ stores them.
block.wareworks.warehouse_interface.tool: The _brass port_ faces the clicked _inventory_, such as a _chest_ or _barrel_. Clicked on the side of another _warehouse interface_, it copies that direction; otherwise it faces away from you. Keep the _framed plate_ towards the _aisle_.

Click the _filter slot_ below the arm port with an item to store _only_ that item here. _List_, _attribute_ and _package filters_ all work, and an _empty_ slot accepts _everything_. A filter only restricts _storing_: whatever is already inside can always be _retrieved_, and changing a filter never moves items that are already stored.

_Hold_ the click on the _filter slot_ to set a _priority_ from _0_ to _9_: among the locations that are _equally suitable_, the crane fills the _highest_ one first, so a rack by the _door_ can fill before the far end of the aisle. It only decides where _new_ items go — it never moves what is already stored, and _retrieval_ always takes the _nearest_ source.
Shows its _address_, its _filter_, its _priority_, the _attached inventory_, its _used slots_, the most stored _items_ and the items _reserved_ for a running crane job.
Turns the _inventory_ it faces into an _addressable storage location_ of a warehouse aisle. A _stacker crane_ stores items there and takes them out again.
block.wareworks.warehouse_output.tooltip: The _opening_ faces you: stand in the _aisle_ and place it into a _rack_ beside the aisle. A new port _requests_, exactly as before.

Click the _filter slot_ with the item to request. It sits on the _top_, the _back_ and both _side_ faces, never in the _aisle opening_, where the crane reaches in. Hold _Right-Click_ on it to set the _amount_ and _when_ the port acts: on a _pulse_, _while powered_, or _unless powered_.

Hold _Right-Click_ with the _wrench_ on the port's own box — a small box on the same _top_, _back_ and _side_ faces, just above the filter slot — to set the _direction_: _Request_, or _Accept_ with a rank. An _overflow_ ranks after every storage location, a _diversion_ before them, and the _filter_ then says which items the port takes at all. An accepting port turns _andesite_ around the aisle opening and on the spout, and shows its rank on the _back_.

A _requesting_ port asks the _warehouse controller_ for the filter item: up to the set _amount_, at most what is _in stock_. An _accepting_ one takes items that arrived at an _input_ and would otherwise be stored. _On a pulse_ it acts once per signal; _while powered_ it keeps going, with _one_ open request at a time, so a machine is fed without a _clock_; _unless powered_ does the same until a _lever_ switches it off. Nothing is ever _destroyed_: a full port lets the _input_ back up.

Shows its _address_, the _buffered items_ and its _redstone_ setting. A _requesting_ port adds its _pending request_ with the items _delivered_ so far and why the last one was _refused_; an _accepting_ one its _rank_, which items it _accepts_ and how many it has _handed over_.
The _port_ of a warehouse _aisle_: it _requests_ items, or it _accepts_ what the warehouse cannot keep. _Funnels_, _chutes_, _hoppers_ and _Mechanical Arms_ can pull them out.
block.wareworks.warehouse_production.too: The _opening_ faces you: stand in the _aisle_ and place it into a _rack_ beside the aisle.

_Right-Click_ with an _empty hand_ to open it. Click a _slot_ with an item to set an _ingredient_ or the _result_, and _scroll_ on a slot to change its _amount_. Nothing is used up: the pattern only says what one run of your machine needs and makes.

The _terminal_ marks a pattern's result as _producible_ even when none is in stock. Ordering it reserves the _ingredients_, the crane delivers them here, and the _product_ returns to the warehouse through a _warehouse input_ like any other item.

If another _pattern_ of the same warehouse makes that ingredient, the whole _chain_ is planned the moment you click: _one order per step_, each at the station holding its pattern, and every _intermediate_ travels through a real _storage location_. A step that is waiting for an earlier one is handed _nothing_ at all. If something is really missing, the click is _refused_ and names the item.

If your machine takes the _ingredients_ and nothing comes back, the warehouse _stops making that item_ and the _ring_ of this block turns into a red _lamp_: nothing takes items back out of a machine, so it never quietly tries again. Look at the machine, then _Sneak-Right-Click_ this block or click the red row in its _screen_ to make the item again — you are told how many _ingredients_ were delivered and never came back.

Shows its _address_, its _patterns_, the running _production orders_ with their _state_ and the _buffered items_. While the warehouse has _stopped_ making something this station makes, it says how many products are held and what they cost.

A _station_ of a warehouse _aisle_ that feeds your _machines_. Define a _pattern_ here, and the _stacker crane_ brings its _ingredients_ to this block; your own _funnel_, _chute_, _belt_ or _Mechanical Arm_ carries them into the machine. Wareworks never crafts anything itself.
block.wareworks.warehouse_rail.tooltip.b: Runs in the direction you look. A _gap_ or another block ends the rails; the _picture_ of a corner or a junction follows the rails around it. Every straight _run_ of rails is one _aisle_ and keeps _one letter_, however many corners and junctions it passes through; a rail that leaves a run sideways starts the _next_ aisle, counted outwards from its _junction_.
_Closes_ the rail and opens it again. A _closed_ rail belongs to no warehouse, which keeps two warehouses whose rails touch apart and sends a _stray_ rail away again.
block.wareworks.warehouse_rail.tooltip.s: Lays out the _aisles_ of a _stacker crane_. Rails that _touch_ connect, so all the rails in front of the crane's _dock_ are its warehouse: it may _bend_ round corners, _split_ into side aisles and even close into a _ring_, and the crane drives all of it.
block.wareworks.warehouse_stock_keeper.t: The _panel_ faces you: stand in the _aisle_ and place it into a _rack_ beside the aisle, like every other station.

_Right-Click_ with an _empty hand_ to open it. Click a _row_ with an item to set what it governs, and _scroll_ on one of its three numbers to change it (_Shift_ for whole stacks, _Right-Click_ to switch it off). Nothing is used up: a row's item is only a name.
The warehouse _tries to keep_ this many. While it holds fewer, the comparator on this block calls for the item, so a _farm_ or a hand-built line runs exactly as long as it is needed.

If a _warehouse production_ of the same warehouse has a _pattern_ for the item, the warehouse _orders it by itself_ while it is below the minimum — never spending what a _reserve_ protects. If a machine _swallows_ a batch and nothing comes back, that rule _stops ordering_ and waits for you: open it and click the rule's _mark_, or _Sneak-Right-Click_ the _warehouse production_ that makes the item, to let it try again.
The warehouse stores _no more_ than this. Above it the _stacker crane_ stops accepting the item and a _warehouse input_ holding it _backs up on purpose_ — that is the rule working, not a jam.

The last items are kept from the warehouse's own _automation_: a _redstone request_ at a _warehouse output_ stops at them. _You_ are not stopped — a request at a _terminal_ is served down to the last item.
Shows its _address_, how many _rules_ it holds and how many of them are _below their minimum_, _at their maximum_, _down to their reserve_ or _paused_ after a lost batch.

Holds the _stock rules_ of a whole _warehouse_: one _item_ per row plus a _minimum_, a _maximum_ and a _reserve_. The three numbers govern three different directions, and a warehouse may hold several keepers.
block.wareworks.warehouse_terminal.toolt: The _screen_ faces you and the _arm port_ the opposite way: stand where you want to read the terminal, with the _aisle_ on the far side of the _rack_. The port then moves to whichever side of the terminal the aisle really is on.
The _wrench_ turns the _screen_ to the next face, never onto the _arm port_: the crane keeps loading the terminal from the _aisle_ while you put the screen where you stand.

The screen lists everything the _warehouse_ holds with the amount that is still _available_. Every request is a normal _retrieval job_: the crane brings the items here, just like a request from a _warehouse output_.

An item your _production stations_ can make is offered even when none is in stock, and one whose _ingredients_ are missing is ordered as a whole _chain_. The terminal shows it as _one line_ with the step that is working; a click on that line lists every _step_ with the _address_ of the machine it runs at, and gives the whole chain up at once.

Put a _clipboard_ with a list of items into the slot beside the buffer and press the _list button_: the warehouse works the list off in _portions_ and _ticks each entry off_ as it delivers it, so the clipboard is the order and its receipt in one. A _Schematicannon_ writes its _material checklist_ onto a clipboard, and a hand-written one works just as well. If the list wants more than the warehouse has, or something would have to be _produced_, it asks first; a _full_ terminal makes it wait rather than refuse.

Shows its _address_, the _buffered items_, the _pending request_ with the items _delivered_ so far, and why the last request was _refused_. A _clipboard order_ adds how many of its entries are done and how much is still to fetch.
When ordering something made of something else
A _station_ of a warehouse _aisle_ with a _screen_: ask for items here and the _stacker crane_ fetches them. _Funnels_, _chutes_, _hoppers_ and _Mechanical Arms_ can pull them out again.

wareworks.ponder.shared.crane_needs_rota: Stacker Cranes need Rotational Force from below
Moving Items with a Stacker Crane
Stacker Cranes store and retrieve items in a warehouse aisle
An aisle is one straight run of Warehouse Rails; a warehouse may have several
Storage sits on both sides of the aisle, on as many levels as the crane can reach
A Warehouse Controller behind the dock keeps the stock and plans every job
Faster rotation moves it faster; without rotation it pauses where it is
It travels along the rails and lifts its carriage to the right level
Then its telescopic arm reaches into the rack and the grabber moves the items
The Mast Height on the dock sets how many levels the crane can reach
wareworks.ponder.tag.warehouse.descripti: Components which store and retrieve items with Stacker Cranes
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_corner.text_1: A warehouse is the Warehouse Rails in front of a Stacker Crane's dock
A Wrench closes a rail: it belongs to no warehouse, which keeps two of them apart and sends a stray rail away
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_corner.text_2: Rails connect wherever they touch, not only in a straight line
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_corner.text_3: Two rails at right angles turn the block they share into a corner
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_corner.text_4: Every straight run is one aisle: the one at the dock is A, the next one B
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_corner.text_5: The machine rolls onto that block, swings a quarter turn and drives on down the next aisle
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_corner.text_6: So items reach every aisle of the warehouse, and one block can collect them all
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_corner.text_7: A rack in the corner works too: it belongs to the aisle it faces away from
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_corner.text_8: It reaches both from the very same block, a quarter turn apart
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_corner.text_9: Its address says which: A-01-05L on aisle A, B-01-00L on aisle B
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_filters.text_: Every storage location has a filter slot on its aisle side
An empty slot accepts everything, which is how every warehouse starts
Click it with an item, and only that item is stored here
List, attribute and package filters work the same way
Dedicated locations fill before any unfiltered one
Changing a filter moves nothing, and what is inside can always be retrieved
An item that matches no filter needs a location without one
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_interface.tex: Any inventory beside the aisle can become a storage location
A Warehouse Interface in front of it turns it into one
Its brass port faces the inventory, its framed plate with the arm slot faces the aisle
Together with the crane's aisle, every location gets an address: aisle letter, level and position
Goggles show that address, the attached inventory and what it stores
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_junction.head: Rails That Split
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_junction.text: One straight run of Warehouse Rails in front of the dock is one aisle
The brass port decides, exactly as in a corner: a rack belongs to the aisle it faces away from
Their addresses say which: A-01-06R on aisle A, C-01-01R on aisle C
Rails may leave that run sideways, in the middle of it and not only at its end
Three rails meet on the block they share: it is a junction, and a position of both aisles
As many side aisles as you like may join the same run
A straight run stays one aisle through every junction, so all of this is aisle A
Every side aisle is one of its own, counted outwards from its junction: B and C
At a junction the machine picks its way: straight over it, or round the bend
So goods from every aisle of the warehouse reach the one block you collect them at
These two racks are twins: each one stands beside the run and beside aisle C at once
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_packages_at_t: A Create Packager behind a Warehouse Output packs whatever the warehouse hands over
Whatever address it carries: the warehouse keeps what was inside and the box is gone
A package is opened whole or not at all, so the input needs room for every stack in it
Engineer's Goggles on either door say what it is doing, and why a package was refused
Its back has to touch the station, and which station that is decides the direction
A port only ever hands items out, so a Packager there can only pack: it cannot be set wrong
A plain sign on the Packager is the address every box it sends will carry
A Smart Observer over the port powers the Packager while anything is waiting there
The crane brings what the port asked for, and the Packager boxes it up
One box holds up to nine stacks, and a door sends about one box a second
A funnel, a chute or a Frogport takes the box from the Packager and sends it on its way
The same Packager at a Warehouse Input is an in door: it takes arriving packages apart
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_port_acceptin: Hold Right-Click on a Warehouse Output with a Wrench, and it accepts items instead of asking
It turns andesite where the crane reaches in, and shows its rank on the back you wire up
A negative rank ranks it after every storage location, so it only gets what cannot be kept
A stock rule's maximum is what makes one necessary: above it no location takes the item
The surplus then leaves through the port instead of backing the input up
Nothing is destroyed: what you build behind the port decides where the items go
Unless powered it needs no wiring at all, and one lever switches the overflow off
A positive rank makes it a diversion instead: then it takes items before they are stored
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_port_collecti: A machine drops its result into a chest of its own, and nothing takes it from there
The Collect row of its board turns the port around: now the warehouse fetches instead of waiting
Copper where the crane reaches in says so, and the port reads the inventory right behind it
The crane reaches through the port into that inventory and stores what it finds
That closes the loop: the crane brings the ingredients and takes the product back
Its filter decides what is fetched at all; without one it takes whatever that side hands out
A port collects only while the warehouse may still store: at a maximum it stops by itself
Unless powered it needs no wiring at all, and one lever stops the fetching
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_port_requesti: Supplying a Machine from a Warehouse
A Warehouse Output asks the warehouse for the item in its filter slot
Hold Right-Click on that slot to set the amount, and on the rows when the port acts
On a pulse it asks once per signal, and the crane brings that one load
While powered it asks again by itself as soon as the last items have arrived
Never more than one trip at a time, so a machine behind it stays supplied without a clock
Switching the signal off stops the next trip; what is already on its way still arrives
Unless powered turns that around: the port then works unwired, and a lever switches it off
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_production.te: A Warehouse Production feeds the machines you build next to it
Its pattern only says what one run of your machine needs and makes; nothing is used up
A terminal offers that result even when the warehouse holds none of it
The controller reserves the ingredients and the crane brings them to the station
Your own funnel, chute, belt or Mechanical Arm carries them into the machine
Wareworks delivers and collects; it never crafts anything itself
The product comes back through an ordinary Warehouse Input, like any other item
The crane stores it, and your waiting request is served from that stock
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_production_ch: A button takes two machines, and this warehouse holds nothing but logs
The buttons come back the same way, and the crane brings them to the terminal
If an ingredient is missing and nothing can make it, the click is refused and names it
The warehouse orders your machines one after the other; it never crafts anything itself
Order the button at a terminal anyway: your patterns can reach it
That one click plans the whole chain: one production order per step, at your own stations
The first step gets its ingredients; the step waiting for it is given nothing at all
Your own funnel, chute, belt or Mechanical Arm carries them into the machine
The planks come back through an ordinary Warehouse Input, like any other item
They are stored in a rack: what a step makes is ordinary stock, not a hand-over
Only now is the second step given its ingredients, out of that rack
and your second machine makes what you ordered
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_requesting.te: Right-click the screen with an empty hand to open the terminal
It lists everything the warehouse holds, and the search box finds an item by name
Click an item for the amount in the field, Shift for a stack, Ctrl for everything
Clicking the same item again grows the open request instead of starting a second trip
The crane fetches the items from the locations that hold them
and drops them into the terminal's own slots
Funnels, chutes, hoppers and Mechanical Arms can pull them out from there
Or put a clipboard in: the whole list is fetched, and each entry ticked off as it arrives
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_restocking.te: The warehouse holds fewer than a rule's minimum, and a station here has a pattern for it
So the warehouse orders it by itself: the same production order, with nobody asking for it
Never out of a reserve: with no ingredients it may spend, the rule waits and says so
Your own machine makes the product, exactly as it does for an order of yours
The product returns through an ordinary Warehouse Input, like any other item
An ordinary job stores it, the minimum is met again and the lamp goes out
If a machine swallows a batch and nothing comes back, that rule stops ordering
Check your machine, then click the rule's mark to let it order again
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_retrieving.te: Items leave a warehouse through a Warehouse Output
Click its filter slot with the item you want
Hold Right-Click on it to set the amount, at most one stack
Every redstone pulse asks the controller for that amount
The crane fetches the items from the location that holds them
and drops them into the output, where funnels, chutes, hoppers and Mechanical Arms pull them out
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_stock_rules.t: A Warehouse Stock Keeper holds the stock rules of its aisle
One row is one item and three numbers, and each number governs a different direction
The minimum is what comes in: below it a comparator on the keeper calls for the item
A farm of yours then runs exactly as long as the warehouse needs it
The maximum is what may be stored: above it the crane stops accepting the item
A Warehouse Input then backs up on purpose: that is the rule working, not a jam
The reserve is what may go out to automation: a redstone request stops at the last items
Only what is above it is fetched; the last ones stay in the rack
You are never stopped: a terminal serves you down to the last one and asks before it does
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_storing.text_: Items enter a warehouse through a Warehouse Input
Belts, funnels, chutes, hoppers and Mechanical Arms can put items in; nothing comes back out
The Warehouse Controller looks for a free storage location and orders a job
The crane drives to the input and its grabber takes the items
It carries them to the chosen location and puts them into the inventory behind it
While free locations are left, every item type gets one of its own
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_terminal.head: Placing a Warehouse Terminal
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_terminal.text: A Warehouse Terminal is placed with its screen facing you
Placed from beside the rack, the controller turns its arm port onto the aisle by itself
Stand where you want to read it: the screen keeps its face, only the port moves
A Wrench turns the screen to the next face, never onto the port, and off the aisle side
Goggles show its address, what was delivered here and why a request was refused
wareworks.production.nothing_stopped: Nothing this station makes is stopped
wareworks.production.resume_hint: Sneak-click the station to make them again
wareworks.production.resumed_lost: The warehouse makes %1$s again; %2$s ingredient items were delivered and never came back
wareworks.rail.closed: Rail closed: no warehouse runs through it any more
wareworks.rail.opened: Rail opened: it joins the rails it touches again
